senses.gloss: f. (= גזרזרא, a reduplic. of גזר; for assimilation of sibilants cmp. Nöld. Mand. Gr. p. 45 sq.) something defective, mutilated ;

a large vessel which turned out defective or unwieldy, by having its handles broken off or being cracked, and is therefore used as a receptacle for refuse, as a pickling pot, as a receiver of drippings from a leaking vessel &c.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 2:6">Kel. II, 6</cite> <he>גס׳ שנמצאת וכ׳</he> (Ar.  a defective vessel found in the furnace (in which vessels are put for baking); Tosef.
B. Kam. III, 10 ואם היתה גסטרה but if the jug turned out a gistra, contrad. to נפחתה.

Ib. אי זו היא גסטרא כל שנסדקין אזניה וכ׳ (Kel. IV, 3 גיס׳ כל שניטלו וכ׳ …) when is a vessel called gistra? When its handles are split (broken off) &c. Ib. 2 גי׳ שנתרועעה וכ׳ if a gistra is broken so as to be no longer a receptacle for liquids, though it may yet receive eatables, it is not susceptible of uncleanness, for there is no fragment of a fragment, i.e. a fragment of a gistra is no longer considered a vessel.
Sabb. 96ᵃ (a leaking gistra is not considered a vessel) because nobody says הָבֵא ג׳ לג׳ bring a g. to be put under a gistra; a. fr.
Ḥull. 21ᵃ; 32ᵇ עשאה ג׳ נבלה if one made an animal a gistra by lacerating some of its limbs, it is considered a carcass.
Ib. 52ᵃ ג׳ קאמריתו ye speak of a maimed body (a rib on each side disjointed)! Ib. 27ᵃ דלא לישוייה ג׳ that in cutting the animal’s throat one must not make it a gistra (by cutting the head off).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 52b:15">Snh. 52ᵇ</cite> <he>דעביד ליה ג׳</he> that the culprit be cut in two.—
<cite ref="Chullin 124a:11">Ḥull. 124ᵃ</cite> <he>דעבדיה ג׳</he> he split the stove lengthwise.—Pl. <he>גִּיסְטְרָאוֹת</he>, <cite ref="C01171"><he>גִּיסְטְרָיוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Kelim Kamma 3:8">Tosef. Kel. B. Kam. III, 8</cite> <he>שרובן מן הג׳</he> for most of the fragments of pottery found in the potter’s place come from misshaped vessels.
<cite ref="Mishnah Makhshirin 2:3">Makhsh. II, 3</cite> <he>ג׳ שישראל וכ׳</he> pots into which Israelites and gentiles cast their refuse.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:1:5">Y. Sabb. III, beg. 5ᶜ</cite> <he>ממלא גִּצְרָא וכ׳</he> one may fill a large pot with hot ashes &c.
